screens_reviewed: Three scroll captures (top/early/end) of app/reports/[submissionId].tsx on an Android tablet in portrait, light theme: report overview header, hero card, Submission details + Context panels, Score by section chart, Score results table, Section weighting, highlights, and comment blocks, with a fixed Share / Back to My Audits footer.
verdict: The report renders cleanly and is fully legible: cards, the grouped bar chart, the score table, and the weighting meters all read well and the fixed footer keeps both CTAs in reach. The screen is responsive-aware (centered content track, flexWrap two-column panels) but is essentially a scaled-up phone layout — on this tablet width the paired InfoPanels/CommentBlocks collapse to a single column, leaving the wide content track underused, and the navigation header shows the raw route path instead of the place name.

critical_issues.issue: The native stack header reads the literal route segment 'reports/[submissionId]' instead of the intended place name / 'Report' title. The screen builds a custom headerTitle via YeeStackHeaderTitle (buildReportHeaderLabels) and app/_layout.tsx registers the route with title: "Report", yet neither is showing — the user sees a developer-facing route path.
critical_issues.evidence: image 13/14/15 header text 'reports/[submissionId]'; reports/[submissionId].tsx:178-190 sets headerTitle via YeeStackHeaderTitle; app/_layout.tsx:1385-1388 sets title: "Report"
critical_issues.fix: Ensure the per-screen Stack.Screen options actually apply on Android (the in-screen <Stack.Screen> can race the root registration). Set a non-empty headerTitle/title at the root registration and confirm headerTitle render runs; verify buildReportHeaderLabels returns a primary string so the header never falls back to the route id.

improvements.location: Submission details + Context (image 13), Highlights + Comment blocks (image 15)
improvements.suggestion: On this tablet width the paired panels wrap to a single stacked column because they rely on flexWrap plus per-child minWidth (InfoPanel minWidth 280, CommentBlock minWidth 250, MetricCard minWidth 150) rather than an explicit tablet grid. The result is a centered phone-width column inside a much wider canvas. Drive column count from layout.isTablet / twoPaneGap so panels reliably sit two-up (and comments 2–3 up) on tablets.
improvements.evidence: reports/[submissionId].tsx:315 XStack flexWrap="wrap" with InfoPanel minWidth:280 (line 541), 413/436 comment XStack with CommentBlock minWidth:250 (line 982); contentMaxWidth 1040–1200 from responsive-layout-tokens.ts:779-780

improvements.location: Headings and body throughout (Report overview 30px, Audit results 28px, card titles 20px, body Paragraphs default)
improvements.suggestion: Headings use hard-coded fontSize values (30/28/24/20/18) and most body text uses Tamagui defaults, none multiplied by TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE (1.3) or designSystem.fontScale. The screen reads as a phone layout enlarged only by viewport, so the type hierarchy is the phone hierarchy. Consider scaling fixed sizes by the tablet base scale for a deliberate large-screen rhythm.
improvements.evidence: reports/[submissionId].tsx:266 fontSize={30}, :523 fontSize={28}, :892 fontSize={20}, :551 fontSize={18}; responsive-layout-tokens.ts:792 TABLET_TYPOGRAPHY_BASE_SCALE = 1.3 is defined but not consumed here

improvements.suggestion: The screen imports the static `designSystem` (light tokens) instead of the live `useDesignSystem()` hook, so it cannot follow the user's theme/font-scale/dyslexia preferences. Fine for this light capture, but it means dark mode and accessibility text scaling never reach this report. Adopt useDesignSystem() like the shared header components do.
improvements.evidence: reports/[submissionId].tsx:19 imports static designSystem; lib/design-system.ts:501 useDesignSystem() is the live alternative used by useYeeStackHeaderOptions.ts:1168

tamagui_notes: design_system_components_used: (none) — this screen hand-rolls every surface (Card, InfoPanel, MetricCard, MetricRow, CommentBlock, ChartBar, ImportanceMeter) as local YStack/XStack with inline borderColor/boxShadow/radii rather than reusing shared ui/* primitives (e.g. Badge/ScaledText in core.md). High duplication risk and it bypasses ScaledText font-scaling.

Spacing mixes Tamagui space tokens (p="$4", gap="$3") with raw pixel literals (minWidth 280/250/150, ImportanceMeter width 22/height 8, ChartBar height 14) — reports/[submissionId].tsx:541, 982, 922, 609-610, 803.

Footer paddingHorizontal uses layout.screenPaddingHorizontal but the scroll content uses getResponsiveContentContainerStyle's adaptive centered gutters; on a wide tablet the footer buttons can sit edge-to-edge while content is centered, a slight misalignment (reports/[submissionId].tsx:462 vs :257).
platform_notes: Android tablet correctly uses bottom tab navigation app-wide ((tabs)/_layout.tsx) — but this is a pushed stack detail route with its own header and a fixed bottom action bar, so Material list-detail (master report list beside detail) is not attempted; acceptable for a drill-in but a missed large-screen opportunity.

Icons are Feather (components/icons.tsx) — BarChart3/CloudOff are platform-neutral, no iOS-only chevrons leaking into the body here; the only chevron is the system back affordance in the native Android header.

Footer paddingBottom uses insets.bottom + 12 (reports/[submissionId].tsx:464); the captured device has the Android nav bar hidden via lib/system-bars.ts, so the two CTAs clear the gesture area. Tap targets: Tamagui Button default height comfortably exceeds 48dp.
Status bar area at top is clear; content sits below the native header so no notch/status-bar overlap.
not_assessable: Exact WCAG contrast ratios (estimated only); the muted green percentage labels and mutedForeground body text appear adequate but were not measured.
Dark theme and accessibility font-scale rendering (screen uses static light tokens; only the light capture is available).
The pending-upload, offline-note, and report-unavailable states (none shown in these captures).
Behaviour of the Share native sheet and 'Back to My Audits' navigation (runtime/cross-screen).
score_rationale: Solid, fully usable report with clean cards, a readable chart/table, and reachable CTAs — 7–8 band. Held to 7 by one real navigation defect (header shows the raw 'reports/[submissionId]' route path) plus large-screen polish gaps: paired panels collapse to a single column so the wide tablet canvas is underused, and fixed-px typography is not scaled for tablet. None are layout-breaking, so it stays out of the 5–6 band.
